title: How Hard Is It to Hide a Bit? Empirical Steganographic Capacity of LLMs Under a Monitor

original_idea.body:
# Empirical Steganographic Capacity of LLMs Under a Monitor

Encoder hides 1-8 bits, decoder recovers, monitor flags; measure capacity-vs-stealth curve.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain to collusion/control safety cases; capacity-vs-stealth curve feeds monitoring design.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inference-only LLM harness with simple schemes; clear methodology for novice+mentor.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused capacity-vs-stealth curve; multiple schemes/monitors add some breadth.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: open models, no internal access, collusion is a neglected >1yr concern.

novelty.reasoning: Steganography under monitors is studied; this capacity-vs-stealth quantification may be partially open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Secret-collusion work exists; the capacity-vs-stealth curve may be open.
